questions.stem: A 49 year old woman has had fever, a dry cough, fatigue and aching muscles for 5 days. For 2 days food has tasted of nothing and she cannot smell coffee. Her temperature is 38.2°C, pulse rate 94 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 96% breathing air. Her chest is clear.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Fever, dry cough, myalgia, fatigue and loss of smell are classic Covid-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2.

steps.x: Fever + dry cough + **anosmia**.

elim: A post-cold productive cough, not anosmia with systemic illness.
Gives facial pain and purulent discharge, not fever with dry cough and myalgia.
Sore throat, lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly in young adults.
Pneumonia with hyponatraemia and diarrhoea; anosmia is not typical.

steps.x: **C. Covid-19.** Anosmia with fever and dry cough = Covid-19.

questions.stem: A 68 year old man has had fever and a dry cough for 8 days and is now breathless. His wife tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 last week. His temperature is 38.5°C, pulse rate 104 bpm, respiratory rate 28 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 89% breathing air. There are bilateral crackles. His chest X-ray (see item resources) is shown.

visual.title: Chest X-ray
visual.caption: Bilateral peripheral mid and lower zone infiltrates.

questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Hypoxia, tachypnoea, crackles and bilateral infiltrates after a Covid contact is Covid-19 viral pneumonia.

steps.x: Covid contact, **hypoxia**, crackles and **bilateral** infiltrates.

elim: No cardiac history; febrile with a positive contact.
Gives lobar consolidation, not bilateral peripheral infiltrates.
Occurs in untreated HIV with very low CD4.
Hilar lymphadenopathy in a well patient.

steps.x: **B. Covid-19 pneumonia.** Bilateral infiltrates + hypoxia = Covid pneumonia.

questions.stem: Five patients test positive for SARS-CoV-2 in the same week. Each has fever and dry cough on day 2.
questions.q: Which patient is at highest risk of severe disease?
o: A 19 year old male student who smokes
A 24 year old woman with eczema
A 40 year old man with hay fever
A 79 year old man with COPD and a BMI of 36
questions.e: Older age, chronic lung disease and obesity are risk factors for severe Covid-19.

clues: fever and dry cough on day 2
steps.x: Look for **age, chronic lung disease, obesity, immunosuppression**.

elim: Young; smoking alone is a lesser risk.

steps.x: **E. A 79 year old man with COPD and a BMI of 36.** Older + COPD + obese = highest risk.

questions.stem: A 36 year old man has a positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR after 1 day of fever and sore throat. He has no other illness but stopped his antiretroviral therapy a year ago. His temperature is 37.9°C and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air.
questions.q: Which feature puts him at highest risk of severe complications?
questions.e: HIV-positive status confers a high risk of severe Covid-19 complications.

steps.x: A young man with **untreated HIV**.

elim: A minor factor compared with untreated HIV.

steps.x: **B. HIV infection.** HIV = high risk of severe Covid.

questions.stem: A 62 year old woman on day 9 of Covid-19 deteriorates despite 15 L/min oxygen via a reservoir mask. Her respiratory rate is 36 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 84%. There are widespread crackles. Echocardiogram shows normal left ventricular function. Her CXR shows bilateral diffuse opacities.
questions.q: Which is the most likely complication?
questions.e: Severe hypoxia with bilateral diffuse opacities and normal LV function is ARDS, a complication of Covid-19.

steps.x: Refractory hypoxia, **bilateral** opacities, **not cardiac**.

elim: Would be focal, not diffuse bilateral.
Normal LV function argues against it.

steps.x: **A. Acute respiratory distress syndrome.** ARDS complicates severe Covid.

questions.stem: A 57 year old man admitted with Covid-19 pneumonia 6 days ago develops sudden right-sided pleuritic chest pain and haemoptysis. He was not prescribed thromboprophylaxis. His pulse rate is 118 bpm, BP 112/70 mmHg and oxygen saturation 88% on 2 L/min oxygen. His right calf is swollen.
questions.q: Which is the most likely complication?
questions.e: Covid-19 causes a hypercoagulable state; sudden pleuritic pain, haemoptysis, tachycardia and a swollen calf mean PE.

steps.x: Sudden pleuritic pain + **DVT** in an inflamed inpatient.

elim: Pleuritic pain, haemoptysis and a swollen calf point to VTE.
Would be gradual, without pleuritic pain or calf swelling.
No calf swelling; haemoptysis less typical.
Would give fever and purulent sputum, not sudden pain with a swollen calf.

steps.x: **D. Pulmonary embolism.** Covid is prothrombotic: think PE.

questions.stem: A 27 year old woman has a sore throat, runny nose and mild dry cough for 2 days. Her flatmate tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 3 days ago. Her temperature is 37.6°C, pulse rate 80 bpm and oxygen saturation 99% breathing air. Her chest is clear.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Covid-19 ranges from mild URTI symptoms to pneumonia; spread by droplets and aerosols from a close contact.

steps.x: Close **contact**, URTI symptoms, normal saturation.

elim: Her chest and saturation are normal.

steps.x: **E. Mild Covid-19.** Mild URTI after a Covid contact = mild Covid.

questions.stem: A 70 year old man with Covid-19 is assessed on day 7 of his illness. He has fever and breathlessness. He is diagnosed with Covid-19 pneumonia.
questions.q: Which is the most likely finding on examination?
o: Tracheal deviation away from the right
questions.e: Examination in Covid-19 pneumonia shows hypoxia, tachypnoea and crackles.

steps.x: Viral pneumonia signs.
**D. Tachypnoea with bilateral crackles.** Hypoxia, tachypnoea, crackles.

questions.stem: A 66 year old woman in intensive care with severe Covid-19 has falling urine output, rising creatinine and confusion. Her BP is 82/48 mmHg on noradrenaline. Her ALT is rising and platelets are falling. Blood cultures are negative.
questions.q: Which is the most likely explanation?
questions.e: An excessive cytokine response in severe Covid-19 can cause multi-organ failure.

steps.x: Kidneys, liver, brain, blood and circulation all failing.

elim: No steroid withdrawal and multiple organs fail.
Gives oedema and proteinuria, not shock.
Needs a toxin-producing infection; cultures are negative.

steps.x: **C. Multi-organ failure from Covid-19.** Severe Covid can cause multi-organ failure.

questions.stem: A 33 year old nurse has fever, myalgia, dry cough and loss of smell for 3 days. She cared for several patients with similar symptoms on a ward without masks during an outbreak. Her temperature is 38.0°C and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Covid-19 spreads by droplets and aerosols; fever, dry cough, myalgia and anosmia is the classic picture.

steps.x: Exposure via **droplets/aerosols** and **anosmia**.

elim: No headache, neck stiffness or rash.
Spread from water systems; anosmia is not typical.
A chronic illness with weight loss and night sweats.

steps.x: **B. Covid-19.** Anosmia + exposure = Covid-19.

questions.stem: A 61 year old man has had fever, dry cough and fatigue for 6 days and has lost his sense of smell. His temperature is 38.3°C and oxygen saturation 95% breathing air. Investigations are shown.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Raised CRP with lymphopenia, fever, dry cough and anosmia fits Covid-19.

steps.x: Anosmia, and the bloods show **lymphopenia** with raised CRP.

elim: Would typically give a neutrophilia, not lymphopenia.

steps.x: **C. Covid-19.** Lymphopenia + anosmia = Covid.

questions.stem: A 52 year old woman has had fever, dry cough and anosmia for 3 days. Her temperature is 38.1°C, pulse rate 90 bpm and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation?
o: SARS-CoV-2 PCR on a nose and throat swab
questions.e: PCR testing for SARS-CoV-2 is the gold standard diagnostic test.

steps.x: Suspected Covid: need the **gold standard**.

elim: Shows complications; does not identify SARS-CoV-2.
Show past infection or vaccination, not acute infection.

steps.x: **C. SARS-CoV-2 PCR on a nose and throat swab.** PCR is the gold standard.

questions.stem: A 67 year old man with confirmed Covid-19 is admitted with fever and breathlessness on day 7. His temperature is 38.4°C and oxygen saturation 93% breathing air.
questions.q: Which pattern of blood results is most likely?
questions.e: First-line bloods in Covid-19 typically show raised CRP and lymphopenia.

steps.x: What do bloods show in Covid?

elim: Typical of pertussis or CLL, not Covid.

steps.x: **D. Raised CRP and lymphopenia.** CRP up, lymphocytes down.

questions.stem: A 74 year old woman with PCR-confirmed Covid-19 needs 3 L/min oxygen to keep her saturation at 94%. Her temperature is 38.2°C and respiratory rate 24 breaths per minute. A chest X-ray is requested.
questions.q: Which is the most likely finding on chest X-ray?
o: Single lobar consolidation with air bronchogram
questions.e: CXR or CT in Covid-19 typically shows bilateral infiltrates.

steps.x: Hypoxic Covid pneumonia: imaging pattern?
**B. Bilateral peripheral infiltrates.** Bilateral infiltrates.

questions.stem: A 59 year old man has had fever, cough and breathlessness for 9 days. Oxygen saturation is 91% breathing air. A rapid antigen test was negative, and a PCR result is awaited. His CT chest shows bilateral peripheral ground-glass opacities.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?
questions.e: Imaging shows bilateral infiltrates but PCR is the gold standard to confirm SARS-CoV-2.

steps.x: Imaging fits Covid; confirm with the **gold standard**.

elim: Helps with bacterial co-infection; does not confirm Covid.

steps.x: **C. Repeat SARS-CoV-2 PCR.** PCR confirms; imaging only supports.

questions.stem: A 64 year old woman is admitted with Covid-19 pneumonia. Her oxygen saturation is 92% breathing air. A full blood count and CRP are sent.
questions.q: Which result is most consistent with her diagnosis?
questions.e: Lymphopenia is the classic blood finding in Covid-19, with raised CRP.

steps.x: Which FBC abnormality is typical?
**C. Lymphocytes 0.5 ×10⁹/L.** Lymphopenia.

questions.stem: A 71 year old man with Covid-19 is breathless on day 8. His respiratory rate is 26 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 90% breathing air with crackles at both bases. PCR was positive on day 2.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate next investigation?
questions.e: Chest X-ray or CT is the second-line test, showing bilateral infiltrates and complications.

steps.x: Diagnosis confirmed; now **image** the lungs.
**A. Chest X-ray.** CXR after PCR to assess pneumonia.

questions.stem: A 30 year old man has had fever, dry cough and anosmia for 2 days. His PCR is positive. He has no medical history. His temperature is 38.0°C, pulse rate 84 bpm, respiratory rate 15 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
questions.e: Mild Covid-19 is managed with supportive care: paracetamol and hydration.

steps.x: **Mild** disease, low risk.
**D. Paracetamol and fluids at home.** Supportive care.

questions.stem: A 73 year old woman with Covid-19 pneumonia needs 4 L/min oxygen to keep her saturation at 94%. Her temperature is 38.3°C and respiratory rate 24 breaths per minute. She is not ventilated.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.e: Patients requiring supplemental oxygen get dexamethasone 6 mg daily with remdesivir.

steps.x: Needs **oxygen** but not ventilation.

elim: Treats bacteria, not the virus or inflammation.
She needs oxygen, so needs more.

steps.x: **A. Dexamethasone 6 mg daily with remdesivir.** Oxygen-requiring Covid = dexamethasone + remdesivir.

questions.stem: A 58 year old man with severe Covid-19 is intubated and ventilated in intensive care. He is receiving dexamethasone and remdesivir. His CRP is 210 mg/L.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate additional treatment?
questions.e: Covid-19 patients requiring ventilation receive tocilizumab.

steps.x: **Ventilated** and inflamed on steroids.

elim: For early mild disease in high-risk patients.

steps.x: **E. Tocilizumab.** Ventilated = add tocilizumab.

questions.stem: A 44 year old woman with HIV has a positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR after 1 day of fever and cough. Her temperature is 37.9°C and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air. She takes no interacting medicines.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
questions.e: High-risk patients such as those with HIV get early antiviral treatment: Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir) and/or remdesivir.

steps.x: Mild but **high risk**, early in illness.

elim: She is high risk and warrants early antiviral treatment.

steps.x: **B. Nirmatrelvir with ritonavir.** High risk early = Paxlovid.

questions.stem: A 69 year old man is admitted with Covid-19 pneumonia needing 2 L/min oxygen. He has started dexamethasone and remdesivir. His eGFR is 75 mL/min/1.73m² and platelets 210 ×10⁹/L. He has no bleeding risk.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate additional treatment?
questions.e: Hospitalised Covid-19 patients get prophylactic anticoagulation such as LMWH because of a high VTE risk.

steps.x: Hospitalised Covid inpatient.

elim: Not used for VTE prophylaxis here.

steps.x: **C. Prophylactic low molecular weight heparin.** LMWH prophylaxis.

questions.stem: A 76 year old woman has had Covid-19 for 6 days. Her daughter calls the GP because she is breathless at rest. Her home pulse oximeter reads 88%. Her respiratory rate is 30 breaths per minute.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate next step?
o: Start nirmatrelvir with ritonavir at home
questions.e: Severe hypoxia or respiratory distress requires hospital admission.

steps.x: **Hypoxic** and tachypnoeic.

elim: Too late and she needs oxygen.

steps.x: **A. Admit to hospital.** Severe hypoxia = admit.

questions.stem: A 65 year old man with Covid-19 is admitted with oxygen saturation 89% breathing air and respiratory rate 26 breaths per minute. His temperature is 38.6°C.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate initial management?
questions.e: Supportive care with oxygen therapy comes first in hypoxic Covid-19.

steps.x: **Hypoxia** first.
**D. Supplemental oxygen to target 94–98%.** Give oxygen first.

questions.stem: A 71 year old man with chronic kidney disease and confirmed Covid-19 is offered nirmatrelvir with ritonavir. He takes simvastatin.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate action?
questions.e: Ritonavir inhibits metabolism (CYP3A4), boosting nirmatrelvir but also raising statin levels, so simvastatin is withheld.

steps.x: Ritonavir **inhibits metabolism**: drug interactions.

elim: Ritonavir is needed to boost levels.

steps.x: **E. Withhold simvastatin while on treatment.** Hold simvastatin on Paxlovid.

questions.stem: A 50 year old woman with Covid-19 has lost her sense of smell and has a dry cough. A student asks how SARS-CoV-2 infects respiratory epithelial cells.
questions.q: Which is the mechanism of cell entry?
questions.e: SARS-CoV-2 binds ACE2 on respiratory epithelium via its spike protein, explaining its tropism.

steps.x: Entry receptor for **SARS-CoV-2**.
**D. Spike protein binding to ACE2.** Spike binds ACE2.

questions.stem: A 67 year old man with Covid-19 needs oxygen and is started on dexamethasone 6 mg daily. A student asks why a steroid helps a viral infection.
questions.q: Which best explains the benefit of dexamethasone?
o: It suppresses the excessive host inflammatory response
questions.e: Severe disease is driven by an excessive cytokine response, which is the rationale for dexamethasone and tocilizumab.

steps.x: Steroid in viral pneumonia: target the **host response**.
**E. It suppresses the excessive host inflammatory response.** Dampen the cytokine storm.

questions.stem: A 60 year old woman admitted with Covid-19 is prescribed enoxaparin. She asks why she needs injections when she is not known to have a clot.
questions.q: Which best explains the prescription?
questions.e: Endothelial injury and inflammation cause a hypercoagulable state, increasing VTE risk, hence prophylactic anticoagulation.

steps.x: Why anticoagulate inpatients?
**A. Covid-19 causes a hypercoagulable state.** Hypercoagulable = prophylaxis.

questions.stem: A 55 year old man in hospital with Covid-19 needing oxygen is given remdesivir. A student asks how it works.
questions.q: Which is the mechanism of action of remdesivir?
questions.e: Remdesivir inhibits viral RNA replication (RNA polymerase).

steps.x: Antiviral mechanism.
**D. Inhibits viral RNA replication.** Remdesivir blocks viral RNA replication.

questions.stem: A 63 year old woman in intensive care with Covid-19 has refractory hypoxia. Post-mortem lung histology later shows hyaline membranes lining the alveoli.
questions.q: Which is the most likely underlying process?
questions.e: The cytokine response causes diffuse alveolar damage with hyaline membranes, progressing to ARDS.

steps.x: Histology of **ARDS**.
**C. Diffuse alveolar damage.** Hyaline membranes = diffuse alveolar damage.
